Crosswalk of counts between two sets of areal units

Source: R/pinpl.R
arwt.Rd

Moves values (counts, populations) kept on one set of units (an old boundary version, say) onto another, through the pairs of a source and a target unit that overlap: each source's value is split among its targets in proportion to area, the size of the overlap (its area, or its population for a population-weighted crosswalk), which assumes the value spread uniformly over the source. Where each source lies in one target (a boundary version that only merges units) the result is exact aggregation and exact is TRUE; splitting a source is an approximation. A source with no pair is lost (lost), and each source's main target (its largest share) maps an old identifier onto the new scheme. The concentration of the result across the targets is reported as the Gini coefficient and the share of the largest top targets.

Usage

arwt(x, from, to, area = NULL, id = names(x), top = c(10, 20))

Arguments

x

The values of the source units: finite numbers.

from, to

The overlapping pairs: the source unit (a label in id) and the target unit of each, as many as there are pairs.

area

NULL to split each source evenly among its targets, or the size of each overlap, from 0.

id

The labels of the source units, one per value of x, each once; by default names(x).

top

The numbers of largest targets whose share is reported: whole numbers from 1.

Value

A list of class arwt: out, a data frame of to and value (every target in a pair, in sorted order); map, a data frame of from, to (its main target) and share; exact; lost; and conc, a named vector: gini and top<k>.

References

Goodchild, M. F. and Lam, N. S.-N. (1980). Areal interpolation: a variant of the traditional spatial problem. Geo-Processing, 1, 297-312.

Examples

# four old units onto three new ones; unit d is split 70/30 by area
arwt(c(a = 120, b = 40, c = 60, d = 100),
     from = c("a", "b", "c", "d", "d"), to = c("N1", "N1", "N2", "N2", "N3"),
     area = c(1, 1, 1, 7, 3), top = 1)
#> arwt: 4 sources onto 3 targets, sources split by overlap
#>  to value
#>  N1   160
#>  N2   130
#>  N3    30
#>   gini   top1 
#> 0.2708 0.5000
